info.name: litellm
info.description:
LiteLLM proxy endpoints for this deployment. Config is in `ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml`; operator guide in `ai/litellm/LITELLM.md`; MCP tool-call orchestration in `ai/litellm/LITELLM_MCP.md`.

Auth model: the collection's default Bearer is `virtual master key` — an sk-… issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys (or `/key/generate`). Admin endpoints (under the `Admin` folder) override at the item level to `litellm master key` — the value of `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `.env`, which `general_settings.master_key` reads via `os.environ`. Never distribute the master key; use it only for key/user/model management.

Set the collection variables `litellm` (base URL — localhost publish is 4001 = `PORT_LITELLM`; on `ai_shared` it's http://litellm:4000), `virtual master key`, and `litellm master key` before running requests.

Models enabled in this deployment (from `model_list`): `kokoro` (TTS, audio), `qwen3.6`, `qwen3.8`, `glm5.2`, `qwen2.5-vl` (image), `claude-sonnet-5` (Anthropic fallback), plus the env-driven default (`DEFAULT_LITELLM_MODEL_NAME`). Context-window fallbacks route qwen3.6/qwen3.8/glm5.2 → claude-sonnet-5 when the request exceeds the local model's window (see `litellm_settings.context_window_fallbacks`).

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Quick start.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or POST /key/generate). Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth. Use this for all runtime / model / pass-through / MCP calls.

The proxy's admin master key — value of `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `.env`, read by `general_settings.master_key` in litellm_config.yaml. Required for /key/*, /user/*, /model/* admin endpoints. Do NOT distribute; scope tokens for downstream services via /key/generate instead.
Virtual-key token returned by POST /key/generate as `key`. Paste in to run /key/info, /key/update, /key/delete without editing each URL.
user_id assigned to a virtual key at creation, or a pre-existing user in the LiteLLM DB. Consumed by GET /user/info.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness / readiness probes. `/health/liveliness` is the container's docker healthcheck target (see LITELLM.md § Health checks). `/health` runs an actual upstream ping against configured models — slower, use for diagnostics not for uptime dashboards.

request.description: Full model-health check — pings every entry in `model_list` and returns healthy/unhealthy counts. Not used by the container healthcheck (which uses /health/liveliness); this exists for operator diagnostics. See LITELLM.md § Health checks.
Cheap liveness probe — does not hit upstream models. This is the endpoint the docker healthcheck targets, per LITELLM.md § Health checks.

Readiness probe — reports whether the proxy has finished startup (config loaded, DB connection to `litellm_db` established per LITELLM.md § Quick start). Use this to gate compose `depends_on` conditions.

item.name: OpenAI-compatible
item.description: The primary API surface. LiteLLM presents an OpenAI-compatible interface in front of vLLM (qwen3.6, qwen3.8, glm5.2, qwen2.5-vl), Kokoro TTS, and Anthropic (claude-sonnet-5 fallback). Models available are those enumerated under `model_list` in litellm_config.yaml. See LITELLM.md § `litellm_config.yaml` settings for the config schema reference.

request.description: Standard chat-completion call. `model` must match a `model_name` in `model_list` — this deployment defines qwen3.6, qwen3.8, glm5.2, qwen2.5-vl (image), claude-sonnet-5, kokoro (audio), plus the env-driven `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MODEL_NAME`. If the request exceeds the model's context window, `litellm_settings.context_window_fallbacks` transparently reroutes qwen3.6/qwen3.8/glm5.2 → claude-sonnet-5. Tool calls are supported but not auto-executed — see LITELLM_MCP.md § Step 1/Step 2 for the tool-call loop.

Kick off an MCP-backed tool call. When an `mcp_servers` entry is configured (e.g. `phoenix`), the model receives the tool definitions automatically and returns `finish_reason: tool_calls` with a `tool_call_id`. LiteLLM does NOT execute the call — copy the id and follow up with the step-2 request below. See LITELLM_MCP.md § Step 1: Send the user message.

Send the tool result back. Replace `CALL_ID_FROM_STEP_1` with the id from the step-1 response, and put the actual MCP-tool result string in the `tool` message's `content`. LiteLLM feeds this back to the model, which returns a natural-language response. See LITELLM_MCP.md § Step 2: Send the tool result back.

OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint. `model` must be a `model_list` entry whose upstream supports embeddings. LiteLLM proxies to whichever upstream the model resolves to; failures return the upstream error verbatim. See LITELLM.md § `litellm_config.yaml` settings.

List models visible to the calling key. Union of the static `model_list` in litellm_config.yaml and any models stored in `litellm_db` (enabled by `general_settings.store_model_in_db: true`). Virtual keys with scoped access only see the models they're allowed to call.

OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech. Routes to the `kokoro` model entry, which points at `http://kokoro-api:8000/v1` with `mode: audio`. Response is binary audio (use Postman's Send-and-Download). Kokoro also exposes an MCP server registered under `mcp_servers.kokoro_tts` — see the MCP folder for that path.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Management endpoints that require the LiteLLM master key. Each item overrides the collection-level Bearer to use `{{litellm master key}}` (value of `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `.env`, read by `general_settings.master_key`). Use these to issue and revoke virtual keys, inspect users, and enumerate model config from the DB. See LITELLM.md § `litellm_config.yaml` settings and the linked LiteLLM Config Settings reference for the DB-backed model-management flow.

request.description: Issue a new virtual key. `models` scopes the key to specific `model_list` entries; omit for all models. Response contains a `key` (sk-…) — paste into the `keyToken` collection variable to run the other /key/* requests, or into `virtual master key` to use it for runtime calls. Requires master key. See LITELLM.md § `litellm_config.yaml` settings for the full option reference.
Inspect a virtual key — allowed models, spend, TPM/RPM limits, expiry, metadata. Requires master key.
Update a virtual key's allowed models, spend cap, limits, or metadata. `key` in body identifies the target — set the `keyToken` variable first. Requires master key.
Revoke one or more virtual keys. Deleted keys stop working immediately — any in-flight requests using them 401 on the next call. Requires master key.

query.description: User id to look up. Set the `userId` collection variable first.

request.description: Look up a user — aggregated spend, list of keys owned, budget/limits. Requires master key.

Enumerate every model known to the proxy — union of `model_list` in litellm_config.yaml plus DB-stored models (`general_settings.store_model_in_db: true`). Includes upstream `api_base`, mode (chat/audio/image), and litellm params. Requires master key so upstream keys are visible.

item.name: Pass-through
item.description: Reverse proxies to internal services declared under `general_settings.pass_through_endpoints` in litellm_config.yaml. Every request keeps the caller's `Authorization` header (`forward_headers: true`) and `include_subpath: true` so anything after the mount prefix is passed through unchanged. This means downstream services see the LiteLLM virtual-key Bearer and can authenticate against it. Five pass-throughs are mounted in this deployment: classifier, madlad, interceptor, roofix, sandbox.

request.description: Pass-through to the classifier service — `pass_through_endpoints` mounts `/v1/classifier` → `http://classifier:8000` with methods GET/POST/DELETE. This is a simple health probe example; anything after `/v1/classifier/` reaches the upstream unchanged.
Pass-through to the MADLAD translation service — `/v1/madlad` → `http://madlad-api:8000` with methods GET/POST. Translation calls (e.g. `POST /v1/madlad/translate`) go through this same mount.

Pass-through to the interceptor (CDP capture service) — `/v1/interceptor` → `http://interceptor:8080` with methods GET/POST/DELETE. Capture calls (`POST /v1/interceptor/capture`) and job endpoints all route through this.
Pass-through to the Roofix ↔ Phoenix bridge — `/v1/roofix` → `http://roofix:8080` with methods GET/POST.

Pass-through to sandbox-runner — `/v1/sandbox` → `http://sandbox-runner:8000` with methods GET/POST/DELETE. Full endpoint catalogue in `ai/sandbox/sandbox-runner.postman_collection.json`; this collection only shows the mount health probe.

item.name: MCP
item.description:
LiteLLM advertises MCP servers to clients (Claude Code, Open WebUI, custom apps) via the `mcp_servers` block in litellm_config.yaml. Each entry is mounted at `/mcp/{key}` — the key MUST match the URL path a client points at. LITELLM_MCP.md explains the tool-call loop; LiteLLM only surfaces the tool definitions to the model — YOU orchestrate the actual tool execution and feed the result back with the `tool` role message.

Mounted MCP servers in this deployment (from `mcp_servers`):
- `kokoro_tts` → http://kokoro-api:8000/mcp (TTS)
- `madlad_translate` → http://madlad-api:8000/mcp (translation)
- `interceptor` → http://interceptor:8080/mcp (CDP capture)
- `sandbox` → http://sandbox-runner:8000/mcp (preview_app + get_sandbox_logs — see the sandbox-runner Postman collection's MCP folder for the FastMCP JSON-RPC calls)
- `phoenix` → env-driven URL, bearer auth via `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MCP_PHOENIX_AUTH_VALUE`
- `gmail` → https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1, OAuth2 (authorization_code, delegated to upstream)

Register these with Claude Code via `claude mcp add --transport http -s user {key} {litellm}/mcp/{key} --header "Authorization: Bearer sk-…"` — see LITELLM_MCP.md § Add MCP Servers to Claude Code.

item.name: Kokoro TTS MCP — claude mcp add (docs)

request.description:
URL to register with Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http -s user kokoro {{litellm}}/mcp/kokoro_tts \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}"

Backed by `mcp_servers.kokoro_tts` → http://kokoro-api:8000/mcp. See LITELLM_MCP.md § Add MCP Servers to Claude Code.

item.name: MADLAD translate MCP — claude mcp add (docs)

request.description:
URL to register with Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http -s user madlad {{litellm}}/mcp/madlad_translate \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}"

Backed by `mcp_servers.madlad_translate` → http://madlad-api:8000/mcp.

URL to register with Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http -s user interceptor {{litellm}}/mcp/interceptor \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}"

Backed by `mcp_servers.interceptor` → http://interceptor:8080/mcp.

URL to register with Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http -s user sandbox {{litellm}}/mcp/sandbox \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}"

Backed by `mcp_servers.sandbox` → http://sandbox-runner:8000/mcp. Exposes `preview_app` and `get_sandbox_logs`. For the underlying FastMCP JSON-RPC transport (initialize / tools/list / tools/call), see the MCP folder of `ai/sandbox/sandbox-runner.postman_collection.json`.

URL to register with Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http -s user phoenix {{litellm}}/mcp/phoenix \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer sk-your-phoenix-auth-value"

Backed by `mcp_servers.phoenix` — `url` from `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MCP_PHOENIX_URL`, bearer token from `DEFAULT_LITELLM_MCP_PHOENIX_AUTH_VALUE`. See LITELLM_MCP.md § Add MCP Servers to Claude Code and § MCP API Token (Phoenix uses browser-based OAuth to mint long-lived tokens).

URL to register with Claude Code:

    claude mcp add --transport http -s user gmail {{litellm}}/mcp/gmail

Backed by `mcp_servers.gmail` → https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 with `auth_type: oauth2`, `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`, and `delegate_auth_to_upstream: true` — LiteLLM does not manage the token; the client completes OAuth against Google directly.
